correctness.rationale: For three plant disappearance indicators Yi, same plant-degree multiset under exchangeable deletion gives equal μ; no isolated pollinators makes E[Y1Y2Y3]=Pr(D=all pollinators) equal across networks. Idempotence gives E[X²]=μ+2B,E[X³]=μ+6B+6p*, yielding Δm3=3(1−μ)ΔVar exactly. Independently exhaustively enumerated 387 connected no-isolate labelled bipartite incidence matrices of m+n≤6, grouped into 44 sorted bidegree signature classes: within each group all exact fixed-k extinction-count distributions coincide, ruling out a reversal. For three plants/four pollinators, G=(A,A,AB,BC), H=(A,B,AB,AC) are connected trees with bidegrees (1,2,3),(1,1,2,2); direct unions yield μ=q+q²+q³, ΔVar=2q²(1−q)² and Δm3=6q²(1−q)²(1−q−q²−q³), unique root q≈0.543689. Exact combinatorial exhaustion supports only <=6 minimality; analytic polynomial proves crossing for all 0<q<1.

originality.rationale: Primary coextinction papers by Memmott–Waser–Price (2004), Burgos et al (2006), and Jones–Zurell–Wiesner (2024) treat removal, robustness and analytic mean extinction. The inspected 2024 article suggests variance as future work; no inspected prior source gives the three-indicator third-central-moment identity combined with sharp seven-vertex matched-degree reversal. Identity alone is elementary and not claimed as novelty.
residual_risks: An unrelated combinatorial literature could encode the three-indicator identity; it is not the purported independent main contribution.
Finite lower bound is for connected bidegree-matched networks with the same guild sizes and an exchangeable deletion law, not all ecological models.
